test_title: PYST 8: SSC CPO - General Knowledge and General Awareness (Held On 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: On which date was the second stage (GS2) for GSLV-F16 (launching NISAR) flagged off?
solution:
The correct answer is __**March 2025**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **Second Stage (GS2)** of the **GSLV-F16** launch vehicle was officially flagged off in **March 2025**, specifically on **March 4, 2025**.

• The flagging-off ceremony took place at the **ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPRC)** located in **Mahendragiri**, Tamil Nadu, marking a critical step in the assembly of the rocket.

• The **GSLV-F16** mission is dedicated to launching the **NISAR** (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) satellite, a major international collaboration between the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** and the **National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)**.

• The **GS2 stage** is a liquid-propellant stage that utilizes the **Vikas Engine**, which is the workhorse of Indian liquid propulsion systems, burning a combination of **UDMH** (fuel) and **Nitrogen Tetroxide** (oxidizer).

• This stage is transported from **Mahendragiri** to the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC) SHAR** in **Sriharikota** for final integration with other stages of the launch vehicle.

 **Additional Information__**

• **NISAR Mission Overview:**

• It is a **Dual-frequency (L-band and S-band)** Radar Imaging Satellite designed to map the entire globe in 12 days.

• The mission aims to provide spatially and temporally consistent data for understanding changes in **Earth ecosystems**, **ice mass**, **vegetation biomass**, and **natural hazards** like earthquakes and tsunamis.

• **GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle):**

• The **GSLV Mark II** is a three-stage vehicle consisting of a solid first stage, a liquid second stage (GS2), and a **Cryogenic Upper Stage (CUS)**.

• The **GS2 stage** provides the necessary thrust after the burnout of the solid boosters to propel the payload into a **Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO)** or **Sun-Synchronous Orbit (SSO)**.

• **IPRC Mahendragiri:**

• It is the lead center for **Liquid Propulsion Systems** and is responsible for the assembly, integration, and testing of liquid engines and stages for ISRO launch vehicles.
